decisions.reason: The leak-prevention constraint does not change the valve mechanism, closed-valve behavior, or controlled flow requirements; the same message already separately updates those dispensing attributes.
Preventing bowl leakage into electronics is distinct from the spout removal, flushing, and residue-cleaning requirements.
The containment decision does not alter the spout's bottom location, barista-facing orientation, pouring goal, or selected design reference.
Requiring the bowl not to leak does not change its capacity or deep-well form; containment is owned by the source Requirement.
Liquid leakage into electronics is a containment issue and does not modify the existing splash-control target during mixing.
The leak-prevention constraint has no necessary effect on the green accent color requirement.
The containment decision does not change the machine name or placard wording.
The bowl sealing constraint does not change the DJ-turntable-inspired visual identity.

The source adds a product containment constraint but does not modify the system-layout deliverable or its selected design direction; duplicating the product constraint into the artifact Requirement is unnecessary.
The source does not select or replace any motor, seal, enclosure, or electrical component, so the component-selection deliverable remains unchanged.
The leak-prevention constraint neither changes the rapid V1 priority nor requires departure from the existing simple off-the-shelf sourcing policy.
Although electronics must be protected from liquid, the source does not change the requested basic wiring-plan deliverable or establish a specific wiring modification.
